description: Strike-step classifier cases (fleet-ops#9291, #9275). Each case runs the work job's own `Strike or requeue` run block from .github/workflows/agent.yml against a fake gh. Worker times are epoch seconds from the real 2026-10-05 overload runs 37267338065 (cap death) and 37276581999 (early failure), public on fleet-ops. A runner that dies mid-worker runs no step at all, so it is not a case here: the sweep requeues it (agent-dispatch.yml stalled and orphans). want: infra | strike | park | skip.

cases.name: timeout-overloaded-load
cases.note: real run 37267338065: Worker failed at 55m08s (the cap) while load1 was 57.43; this misstrike hit #9268

cases.name: timeout-overloaded-swap
cases.note: same cap death with a healthy load1 but 7.5G swap in use

cases.name: timeout-healthy
cases.note: cap death on a healthy host is still a strike

cases.name: timeout-no-guard-sample
cases.note: the Host sample never ran: guard unknown, strike (fail-safe)

cases.name: timeout-no-end-time
cases.note: no end time recorded: elapsed unknown, strike (fail-safe)

cases.name: worker-failed-early-overloaded
cases.note: real run 37276581999 leg: a Worker failure after 20 min stays a strike even under overload

cases.name: worker-cancelled-overloaded
cases.note: a cancelled Worker is a strike here; a dead runner is the sweep's job (fleet-ops#9275)

cases.name: later-step-failed
cases.note: Worker succeeded; a later step failed is out of scope, strike

cases.name: second-infra-still-requeues
cases.note: infra says nothing about the packet, so a second infra death requeues instead of parking

cases.name: second-strike-parks
cases.note: existing behavior: the second strike parks with needs-orchestrator

cases.name: displaced-run-skips
cases.note: existing behavior: a run that never claimed the issue is skipped
